chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qassani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isbahani, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the expiation of a vow, so he said: 'The expiation of a vow is like the expiation of an oath. And whoever vows to sacrifice a young camel, upon him is a full-grown camel which he should equip and shear and stop with at Arafat. And whoever vows to sacrifice a sheep, he may slaughter it wherever he wishes.'

key_terms.بِعَرَفَةَ: At Arafat (the site of Hajj standing)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for fulfilling a vow in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the expiation for a vow (*kaffarat al-nadhr*) mirrors that of an oath (*kaffarat al-yamin*), a ruling that distinguishes vows from simple promises. The text provides specific ritualistic details for camel vows, requiring the animal to be equipped and presented at Arafat, while sheep vows allow for flexible slaughter locations, reflecting the jurisprudential nuances in Shia fiqh regarding vow fulfillment.
